newsitem.title: CHINA: China banks call for national credit rating system.
newsitem.headline: China banks call for national credit rating system.

text.p: China should create a unified rating system for domestic firms to give banks a common standard by which to evaluate companies that apply for loans, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
"To date, there has been no such national criterion for assessing the reputation of enterprises in China, owing to the long established planned economy," Xinhua said quoting banking officials.
That had resulted in numerous bad loans and many cases of bad credit, the agency quoted the bankers as saying at a national financial meeting held last week.
Credit ratings for Chinese firms and banks now rely on international organisations that evaluate enterprises based on their relationship with the central government, it said.

"These ratings cannot reflect the real situation in China's banking industry, the country's ongoing banking reform and its efforts to commercialise and internationalise the state-owned commercial banks," Xinhua quoted one banker as saying.
Ratings for state-owned commercial banks have fallen since 1994 when Beijing set up three policy banks as part of a plan to separate policy loans from commercial loans, Xinhua said.
Policy banks such as the Import and Export Bank of China were rated as AA-, the same rating as the Chinese government, it said, without giving further details.
